title: Insurance and Cord Blood Banking
summary: Learn about who may be eligible for insurance to cover some portion of the cord blood banking expense in this article.
body_markdown:
Many parents are now becoming aware of the importance of cord blood banking. Cord blood that is banked can be used by the child or any sibling, so long as they are a match. This is a great option for families who want to be prepared for the future, but it is important to consult with your insurance company to find out if coverage is available.


### Health insurance coverage


There are a few things to keep in mind when it comes to insurance and cord blood banking. First, not all insurance companies cover cord blood banking. Some may only cover donated cord blood, while others may cover the storage and preservation of umbilical cord blood but not its use. It is important to check with your insurance company in order to find out if cord blood banking is covered.


Secondly, there are health reimbursement arrangements (HRAs) and health insurance policies (HIPs) that will reimburse individuals for the costs associated with cord blood banking. If you are interested in cord blood banking, it is important to speak with your HR professional or health insurance company to find out if this is an option for you.


Lastly, it is important to keep in mind that insurance companies may have restrictions on who can bank cord blood. For example, many insurance companies may not cover cord blood banking for parents who are pregnant. If you are pregnant and would like to bank your cord blood, you will need to find a cord blood bank that is compliant with your insurance company’s guidelines. The good news is that there are many options when it comes to cord blood banking.


### Does insurance cover blood banking?


Many insurance companies are starting to cover cord blood banking. This is due to the fact that cord blood has been shown to be a valuable resource for treating a variety of diseases. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends that all parents be informed about the option to bank their child’s cord blood.

### Health reimbursement arrangements


Health insurance policies typically have certain provisions for reimbursement of health care expenses associated with a particular illness or disease.


Cord blood banking may be considered a preventive measure by some insurance companies and therefore not subject to such provisions.


However, families with a history of leukemia or another condition where a stem cell transplant is a standard treatment, and an immediate need for a transplant, may be eligible for insurance to cover some portion of the cord blood banking expense.
